subject: Urgent: Zenport AZ2 traffic surge — request for cross-region rehome and exec sign-off
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenport.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenport.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T02:14:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] us-east-1 AZ2 5xx spike — asking for traffic rehome + exec brief

Stephanie / Marissa —

We're seeing an abrupt, sustained increase in 5xxs and p95 latency starting ~01:50 PDT across our primary traffic routed to us-east-1 AZ2. Error rate is ~18% for the last 6 minutes with request latencies spiking from ~120ms to >1.5s. Our on-call has tried standard retries and soft restarts; the behaviour looks like worker eviction + network instability within the AZ rather than application-level regressions.

Can Redwood initiate an emergency cross-region rehome to us-west-2 (we're asking for 60-80% shift) while we run a forensic on our side? This is impacting checkout flows for several enterprise customers. We need a short executive note (for our CEO and infra leads) confirming Redwood's intended actions and an ETA for stabilization.

Attached a small sample of 500 payloads and logs. We'll provide any additional telemetry you need. Please treat as P0 — we will escalate internally as well.

Attachments: zenport-500-sample.log (text)

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform, Zenport AI
alex.turner@zenport.ai
Office: +1 415 555 0123

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenport.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenport.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T02:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: [URGENT] us-east-1 AZ2 5xx spike — asking for traffic rehome + exec brief

Team — forwarding Zenport P0. They want an emergency cross-region rehome to us-west-2 (target 60-80%). Can SRE confirm feasibility + estimated time-to-activate?

Key asks from Zenport:
- Rapid shift of traffic away from AZ2 to us-west-2 (canary then ramp)
- Short exec note for their leadership confirming our actions and any SLA/credit implications
- An ops play that minimizes KV cache cold-start pain (they use Redis-backed prefix caching)

Logan / Marcus: please include what we need to do from the routing side (smart routing policy change, cache-warm strategy) and a recommended rollback plan. I can own the external comms and exec note.

Stef
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenport.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenport.ai>, aws-support@amazon.com
Date: 2027-08-16T03:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] us-east-1 AZ2 5xx spike — asking for traffic rehome + exec brief

Stephanie / all —

Quick technical triage: initial telemetry shows elevated worker eviction rates and TCP resets concentrated on AZ2 hypervisor subnet. Instance health checks are flapping; we have transient 502/503 returning from the inference runtime, not model outputs. This matches a localized network-plane disturbance rather than an application regression.

Recommended immediate action (safe, reversible):
- Activate routing policy "zenport-emergency-08-16" to steer 70% traffic to us-west-2 (route-level override at the edge proxy). Keep 30% to us-east-1 for continuity and monitoring.
- Pre-warm KV cache: spawn a small warmup fleet in us-west-2 and prefetch the top-1000 prefixes using Zenport's hottest keys (Zenport provided sample). This reduces cold-start tail latency risk.
- Apply concurrency cap in us-west-2 for the first 10 minutes (to avoid amplifying unseen downstream issues).
- Enable request-level observability (trace sampling up to 100% for this route).

Estimated times:
- Config deploy + canary (10% -> 70% within 12 minutes): ~15 minutes to partial, 30 minutes to full ramp if metrics stable.
- KV cache warm: initial warm hits within ~8 minutes after prefetch.

Risks: token-cost delta due to double writes & warmup traffic; brief extra egress charges during data transfer for warmed caches; potential for skewed latency if us-west-2 experiences unexpected load.

I have opened an AWS support ticket (PD-987654) to rule out hardware/network infra issues in us-east-1 AZ2.

Logan
Logan Wright
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: traffic-steer-snippet.yaml (text)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenport.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenport.ai>
Date: 2027-08-16T04:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] us-east-1 AZ2 5xx spike — asking for traffic rehome + exec brief

Stephanie — technical playbook (short):

1) Canary plan
- Route 10% off AZ2 -> us-west-2 for 8 minutes. Monitor 5xx, p99 latency, and error composition.
- If stable (<1% 5xx and p99 within +25% of baseline), ramp to 70% over next 10 minutes.

2) Cache handling
- Spin up 4 cache-warm workers in us-west-2 (small), prefetch top keys Zenport provided; use a low-priority background job to populate local KV layer.
- Do not invalidate global KV; instead use a read-through preference for us-west-2 until warmed.

3) Fallback and rollback
- If 5xx > 5% or p99 > 2x baseline at any canary step, revert to original routing and run deeper infra checks.

4) Executive ask (from us to Zenport)
- Approval for temporary cross-region shift and acknowledgement of resulting transient cost delta (we estimate +12% token/egress cost for the event window; we can discuss a goodwill credit separately).

I can run the traffic steer once we get the yes. I will prepare the exact command set and a one-click rollback.

Marcus Lin
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@zenport.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zenport.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T05:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [URGENT] us-east-1 AZ2 5xx spike — request for cross-region rehome + exec brief

Alex / Priya —

Quick summary and decision: Redwood will proceed with a controlled cross-region rehome to us-west-2 (canary -> ramp) per Logan and Marcus's plan. Implementation timeline: we started the canary at 04:35 PDT (10% to us-west-2). Marcus ran the warm-up job and the initial telemetry looks good — 5xx at canary slice is currently 0.6% and p99 is within +18% of baseline. We will ramp to 70% by 04:50 PDT if the next 10-minute window remains stable.

Operational notes for your leadership:
- We anticipate a short cost delta due to cache warm and redirected egress; estimate ~+12% for the event window.
- We will keep 30% on us-east-1 for visibility and implement automatic rollback conditions.
- AWS support ticket PD-987654 is open to investigate the AZ2 substrate instability.

Next steps we are taking now:
- Continue to monitor traces and heatmap; we'll send a 30-minute exec update once ramp completes.
- Post-incident we'll share a short RCA and any runbook updates.

If you'd like an internal exec note we can share with your CEO, I can draft and send in the next 20 minutes. 

Stef
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: steer-playbook.pdf
